title: Token leak detection and traffic suppression digest
content:
Summary:

A low-and-slow token leak was detected over a 36-hour window starting 2026-02-16 07:20 UTC. The leaked API key was being used by a distributed set of clients to send steady small bursts (40-200 requests/min per node) which individually stayed under per-key rate limits but collectively created a prolonged quota exhaustion signature for a subset of critical routes (generation endpoints with long sequences).

Why this document exists:
- Capture detection signals that mattered (what alerted us).
- Record immediate containment steps and heuristics used.
- Draft a practical runbook for the next occurrence with concrete commands and thresholds.
- List follow-ups for engineering and product to avoid recurrence.

What alerted us:
- Automatic SLO alarm: 95th percentile latency on text-generation-p1 spiked by 45% over baseline for >30m (alert SLO-1134).
- Token exhaustion metric: per-tenant token budget burn rate increased across 23 tenants that share the same default quota-cache shard (metric: quota.burn_rate_shard_7 > 1.4x baseline).
- Unusual client fingerprint signal: identical Accept-Language and empty Referer headers from dozens of IPs with rotating UA strings.
- Spike in 429s with no correlated traffic source from customers' monitored apps (customer CS reports).

Immediate triage timeline (concise):
- 2026-02-16 07:28 UTC: Pager escalated to on-call SRE (Marcus).
- 07:35: Quick check: global infra healthy, no cluster restarts (k8s events normal).
- 07:45: Identified top-20 keys by request volume for the past 2 hours. One key (key_ak_12xxxx) accounted for 39% increase across the affected shard.
- 08:02: Throttle rule applied: per-key soft cooldown (60s/req -> 300s cooldown if burst>500 in 10m) via rate-limiter config (runtime flag: rl.suppress_soft_cooldown=true).
- 08:15: Applied WAF rule to block requests with header pattern: Accept-Language matching "^.{0,3}$" AND Referer empty (WAF rule id waf-2396).
- 09:00: Requested customer key rotation (KMS) and rotated suspected leaked key.
- 11:00: Observed traffic fall to baseline; continued monitoring for 48h.

Triage notes and heuristics used:
- Key fingerprinting: grouped requests by (api_key, first_8_chars_of_user_agent, Accept-Language, Referer, ip_asn). Generated a similarity score and used clustering to detect distributed use of single key.
- Per-key vs shard metrics: when per-key rate was under limit but shard burn was high, we flagged multi-key collusion. Useful boolean: shard_burn > 1.2 && count_unique_keys_in_shard > 15 && median_per_key_qps < configured_hard_qps -> likely leak + botnet.
- Latency correlation: Long-seq generations (>=1024 tokens) contributed disproportionally to quota burn. Prioritize protecting high-cost routes with separate quotas.

Containment recipe (to be elevated into runbook):
1) Detection: run quick query to list top keys for last 2h: 
   - curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API_TOKEN" "https://telemetry.internal/api/v1/metrics/top_keys?window=2h&metric=requests"
2) If single key accounts for >30% of spike: issue immediate rotation via KMS. If rotation not possible immediately, proceed to step 3.
3) Apply tiered per-key suppression:
   - soft cooldown: allow current connections to finish, set per-key delay to 300s for new requests from that key.
   - hard block: if key issues >1000 requests in 1h after soft cooldown, automatically blacklist at WAF.
4) Apply WAF temporary signatures focusing on header/user-agent anomalies. Example regex used in incident: 
   - User-Agent fuzz pattern: "bot-?[0-9a-f]{6,}" or UA strings containing only hex/alpha sequences longer than 12 chars.
   - Block rule: (Accept-Language == "") && (Referer == "") && (UA matches regex) -> action=challenge/block.
5) Shard load relief: move critical tenants to alternate quota shard if shard_burn remains >1.3 after immediate measures.
6) Customer communications: CS template to notify affected customers and explain key rotation + protective measures.

Commands and quick snippets used (copyable):
- Top keys (SQL style):
  SELECT api_key, count(*) AS reqs, sum(tokens) AS tokens FROM requests WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '2 hours' GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 50;
- Rotate key (KMS CLI):
  kms rotate-key --key-id key_ak_12xxxx --reason "suspected leak" --owner "SRE team"
- Apply temporary WAF rule (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $WAF_TOKEN" -d '{"match": "(accept-language==\"\") && (referer==\"\") && user_agent_regex==\"^([a-f0-9]{12,}|bot-[0-9a-f]+)$\", "action":"block", "ttl_minutes":240}' https://waf.internal/api/rules

Open questions and unresolved hypotheses:
- Did the leak originate from a staging leak vs production secret exposure? Need to cross-check deploy logs and infra audit logs for stdout scraping around 2026-02-15 22:00-02:00 UTC.
- Why were some long-sequence requests successful and others rate-limited? Potential bug in token-charging logic for cached responses (checking with infra-team).
- Could attackers have been deliberately shaping Accept-Language/Referer to avoid simple UA-based detectors? Consider adding entropy checks on header distributions.

False positives observed during containment:
- Some SDK versions used by legitimate customers generate compact Accept-Language fields and no Referer (server-side SDK). WAF rule initially impacted 2 legitimate customers; rollback was quick after CS flagged them. Lesson: always check customer SDK fingerprint map before full block.

Post-incident follow-ups (owners assigned):
- eng-sre: formalize and publish the "per-shard leak detection" alert rule (SRE-5872) and add a higher-confidence clustering step to reduce FP. (Owner: Marcus)
- infra: audit token-lifecycle codepath for possible leakage from deploy logs and ensure secret-masking on agent side. (Owner: Rina)
- product: evaluate splitting high-cost generation routes into separate quota buckets to prevent cross-shard exhaustion. (Owner: Diego)
- devexp: update SDK docs to recommend default headers to reduce ambiguity in fingerprinting and add a header entropy metric. (Owner: Aisha)
- cs: prepare customer-facing postmortem template and run through legal for wording around leaked credentials. (Owner: Priya -- customer-success)

Metrics to collect for next 90 days:
- per_key_burn_rate (1m/5m/1h) 
- shard_unique_key_count (1m/5m)
- header_entropy_score per request source (5m)
- long_sequence_token_fraction per tenant (1h)
- waf_challenge_false_positive_rate (daily)

Runbook draft entries to formalize:
- detection queries + thresholds (copy exact SQL/PromQL)
- escalation matrix for CS + legal + infra (who to ping at what thresholds)
- rollback steps for accidental false positives (how to remove waf rule fast and communicate)
- automation: add a run() task in ops-playbooks to perform safe key rotation via KMS with an approval flow.

Notes to self (on-call shorthand):
- prioritize rotating keys over long-term throttling when single key is clear culprit. Rotation mitigates the distributed botnet quickly.
- if multiple keys involved but pattern matches a single SDK fingerprint, work with DevExp to notify SDK owners and push patch.
- always keep a list of 3 alternate quota shards to move critical tenants to; maintain a warm reserve capacity for emergency relief.

Draft status and next steps:
- This doc is a working digest intended to be converted into two artifacts: (1) a short runbook checklist for on-call and (2) a longer postmortem to publish to Confluence.
- Next sync: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC with eng-sre + infra to finalize detection queries and automation tasks.

Appendix: quick reference thresholds (for quick copy into pager messages)
- pager -> severity 1 if shard_burn > 1.4 AND affected_tenants > 5 AND median_latency_increase > 25% for 15m.
- notify legal if customer data exfil suspicion arises OR if keys tied to paid enterprise customers were leaked.
- auto-rotate if single key accounted for >35% of tokens in 2h window.

End of digest.

-- Marcus (oncall, eng-sre)
